name: Tim Dooley Atlas — Unified Manifest
purpose: Canonical map of the repository. The public index is the single human entry point; modular data remains behind it so useful information can stay dense without multiplying interfaces.
navigation_rule: Do not maintain parallel public readers for the same corpus. The index opens records in place and exposes source files when useful.
architecture_rule: One body of knowledge, many data structures, one public Door. Canonical records own definitions; evidence, chronology, research and relationships add context without becoming duplicate identities.
information_principle: Maximize useful information per surviving artifact. Prefer a thick canonical record over several shallow wrappers or generated snapshots.
consolidation_rule: One concept has one canonical identity and definition owner. Other appearances are evidence, occurrence, research, relationship, chronology or projection.
fallback: Local repository data remains available when optional live enrichment fails.
anti_clutter_rule: A file earns existence only when it owns distinct valuable information, primary-source material, a reusable schema, a necessary index, or a real executable function. Placeholder scaffolds, generated snapshots, stale route maps and duplicate wrappers are removed or consolidated.
